To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The risk of the producer is always less than the consumer's risk; (2) The risk of a producer is less than the consumer risk when the test limit is less than the mean value of the measurement errors; (3) The risk of both the producer and the customer is less than 50% when the test limit lies in the interval between the mean value of measurement errors and the true quality characteristic; (4) The risk of producer is greater than the customer risk
the risks for the consumer and the producer are not equal, but depend on the size of the measurement error.
the producer and the consumers risks for asymmetrical test limits are different from those for symmetrical test limits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to define and compute the risks for the producer and the customer when test and specification limits are not symmetrical.
the problem of the determination of the producer and consumer risks in the case of asymmetrical test and specifications limits.
the problem of how to determine the test and specification limits in a production process when the producer and consumer risks are known.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risks are not greatly affected by the degree of asymmetry of the limits, but are very dependent on the size and position of the limits.
the producer risk is generally higher for asymmetrical test limits than it is for symmetrical test limits.

, in general, asymmetrical test and spec limits are preferable to symmetrical ones, and that, in the case of a given asymmetrical test limit, the consumer risk is reduced if the specification limit is made more asymmetrical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risks are smaller for asymmetrical test or specification limits than for symmetrical limits, and the difference is greater the larger the measurement error.
the producer and the customer risks for asymmetrical test limits are higher than for symmetrical test limits.
the producer and the consumers' risks are functions of the test and specification limits and the distribution of the measurement error.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumer risk can be reduced by increasing the test limit.
the risk of the producer and the risk of the consumer are not necessarily equal.
asymmetrical test and spec limits are more effective than symmetrical limits in controlling the risks of the producer and the customer.
